lesson_flow.title: Let's Learn Shapes!
lesson_flow.narration: Hello! I'm your shape friend. Today we are going to learn about circles, triangles, rectangles, and squares. Are you ready to be a shape detective?

interactions.feedback_incorrect: Let's try again. Tap the button to begin.

lesson_flow.title: Our Goal
lesson_flow.narration: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to name and find circles, triangles, rectangles, and squares in the world around you.
lesson_flow.on_screen_text: Our Goal: Name and find circles, triangles, rectangles, and squares.

lesson_flow.title: Circle
lesson_flow.narration: This is a circle. A circle is round and has no corners. Look at the ball, the plate, and the sun. Can you tap on the circles in the picture?

interactions.feedback_incorrect: That's not a circle. Try again.

lesson_flow.title: Triangle
lesson_flow.narration: This is a triangle. A triangle has three sides and three corners. Look at the pizza slice, the traffic sign, and the cracker. Can you tap on the triangles in the picture?

interactions.feedback_incorrect: That's not a triangle. Try again.

lesson_flow.title: Rectangle
lesson_flow.narration: This is a rectangle. A rectangle has four sides and four corners. Opposite sides are equal. Look at the book, the door, and the window. Can you tap on the rectangles in the picture?

interactions.feedback_incorrect: That's not a rectangle. Try again.

lesson_flow.title: Square
lesson_flow.narration: This is a square. A square has four equal sides and four corners. Look at the chess board, the window pane, and the tile. Can you tap on the squares in the picture?

interactions.feedback_incorrect: That's not a square. Try again.

lesson_flow.title: Space
lesson_flow.narration: Space is the area where we can put things. This box has space inside. We can put shapes in the space. Let's drag the shapes into the box.
lesson_flow.on_screen_text: Drag the shapes into the box.

interactions.prompt: Drag a shape into the box
interactions.feedback_correct: Great! You put the shape in the space.
interactions.feedback_incorrect: Try dragging the shape into the box.

lesson_flow.title: Long and Round
lesson_flow.narration: Some objects are long (like a pencil) and some are round (like a ball). Let's play a game: I'll show you an object, and you tell me if it's long or round.

interactions.prompt: Tap 'long' if the object is long, or 'round' if it is round.
Tap 'long' if the object is long, or 'round' if it is round.

lesson_flow.title: What Did You Learn?
lesson_flow.narration: Let's think: What is your favorite shape? Where did you see it today?
lesson_flow.on_screen_text: Think about your favorite shape and where you see it.

lesson_flow.title: Let's Remember
lesson_flow.narration: Today we learned about circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, space, long and round. You did a great job!
lesson_flow.on_screen_text: Great job! You learned about shapes and space.

lesson_flow.title: Shape Quiz
lesson_flow.narration: Let's see what you remember. I'll ask you a few questions.
lesson_flow.on_screen_text: Question 1: What shape has no corners?

interactions.feedback_correct: Correct! A circle has no corners.
interactions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. A circle has no corners. Try again.

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to name and find circles, triangles, rectangles, and squares in the world around you.
This is a circle. A circle is round and has no corners. Look at the ball, the plate, and the sun. Can you tap on the circles in the picture?
This is a triangle. A triangle has three sides and three corners. Look at the pizza slice, the traffic sign, and the cracker. Can you tap on the triangles in the picture?
This is a rectangle. A rectangle has four sides and four corners. Opposite sides are equal. Look at the book, the door, and the window. Can you tap on the rectangles in the picture?
This is a square. A square has four equal sides and four corners. Look at the chess board, the window pane, and the tile. Can you tap on the squares in the picture?
Space is the area where we can put things. This box has space inside. We can put shapes in the space. Let's drag the shapes into the box.
Some objects are long (like a pencil) and some are round (like a ball). Let's play a game: I'll show you an object, and you tell me if it's long or round.
Let's think: What is your favorite shape? Where did you see it today?
Today we learned about circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, space, long and round. You did a great job!
Let's see what you remember. I'll ask you a few questions. Question 1: What shape has no corners?

validation_requirements: Each learning objective must be addressed by at least one screen.
Each major concept (circle, triangle, rectangle, square, space, long, round) must have at least one illustration.
Each screen must have a clear purpose.
The lesson must include at least one teacher interaction (audio narration) and one student interaction (tap, drag, etc.) per major concept.
The lesson must end with a summary and a transition to the next lesson (implied by the quiz and then we would go to next lesson).
The experience must be engaging for a Grade 1 student (short screens, rich illustrations, frequent encouragement).
